`@auto` walks up from the edited file to the tree root looking for a manifest. This tree has none, so the checker is skipped by name and the edit is kept, like any other skipped check.

```console
$ lets edit usage.ts --old 'const cap = 10' --new 'const cap = 20' --check @auto
── usage.ts · 1 replacement · line 6 · check: structure ok · sha:c5525cc20b61→419c5d6249b3 · check: skipped (@auto found no manifest)

```

The control for `check-cargo-workspace-reverts`: the same workspace-wide check over an edit `b` still compiles against passes, and the edit is kept.

```console
$ lets edit a/src/lib.rs --old 'n * 2' --new 'n + n' --check @cargo
── a/src/lib.rs · 1 replacement · line 2 · check: cargo check --workspace --quiet --all-targets ok · sha:[..]

```

`@cargo` runs in `a/`, the nearest `Cargo.toml`, and checks the whole workspace: `b` calls `a::double`, so renaming it in `a` alone passes a check of `a` and breaks `b`. The preset passed before the edit and failed after it, so the file is restored and the `.out` tree shows its original bytes. The sibling `.requires` names `cargo`, and the case is skipped by name on a box without it.


The same plaintext match, `#greet`, has a brace-matched end (`end_guessed` false), so
`--insert-after` applies it rather than refusing.

```console
$ lets edit greet.kt --insert-after '#greet' --new '// end greet'
── greet.kt · inserted 1 line after #greet (line 6) · sha:28d97b9d9e49→7732f6bba255 · check: skipped (no grammar for .kt)

```

`#limit` is a single-line plaintext match with no brace body, so its end is a guess
(`end_guessed` true). `--insert-after` refuses before any write rather than anchoring on a
guessed line, and names a command that anchors on the guessed span's last line instead. The
anchor is wildcarded because trycmd reads its backslashes as path separators;
`insert_after_line`'s unit tests pin its exact text, and `tests/cmd.rs` runs the command.

```console
$ lets edit greet.kt --insert-after '#limit' --new '// upper bound'
? 1
greet.kt#limit: the end of this symbol is a guess (plaintext heuristic) · use --insert-before, or anchor on its last line: lets edit greet.kt --insert-after [..] --new '// upper bound'
ERROR_CODE=guessed_span

```

A `.kt` file has no bundled grammar, so `#greet` resolves through the plaintext heuristic
instead of raising `no_grammar`; `--insert-before` never checks `end_guessed`, so a brace-bodied
match applies like any tree-sitter symbol.

```console
$ lets edit greet.kt --insert-before '#greet' --new '// prints a greeting'
── greet.kt · inserted 1 line before #greet (line 3) · sha:28d97b9d9e49→eebd063aa6ca · check: skipped (no grammar for .kt)

```

A file with no bundled grammar still fails the way a tree-sitter miss does when no plaintext
heuristic matches, and the message hands back the `@'regex'` form the miss cannot rule out.

```console
$ lets edit greet.kt --insert-before '#nope' --new '// unreachable'
? 1
#nope (try @'nope') not found in greet.kt
ERROR_CODE=not_found

```

`#limit` in a `.kt` file resolves through the plaintext heuristic, and with no brace body its end
is a guess, so `--old` searched a span that may be wrong: the header says so where `show` names
its heuristic, and `--json` carries it under the same `resolver` key.

```console
$ lets edit 'greet.kt#limit' --old 20 --new 30
── greet.kt · 1 replacement · line 8 · exact · span guessed (plaintext heuristic)
7 	
8~	val limit = 30
── sha:28d97b9d9e49→d160887527f5 · check: skipped (no grammar for .kt)

$ lets edit 'greet.kt#limit' --old 30 --new 40 --json
{"path":"greet.kt","replacements":1,"lines":[8],"match":"exact","resolver":"span guessed (plaintext heuristic)",[..]}

```

The control for `plaintext-scoped-guessed-span`: a `#symbol` the TypeScript grammar resolves has
a parsed end, so the same scoped edit names no guessed span in text or `--json`.

```console

{"path":"usage.ts","replacements":1,"lines":[2],"match":"exact","region":[..]}

```

A comment describing the next table is a tree-sitter "extra" that would otherwise attach to the
table before it; `[package]` still ends at its last key/value line, so the insert lands before
the blank line and the comment, and the comment stays with `[deps]`.

```console
$ lets edit t2.toml --insert-after '#package' --new 'version = "2"'
── t2.toml · inserted 1 line after #package (line 2) · check: toml ok · sha:970412923003→f01028e03598

```

A table's span now stops before the next table's header (`src/symbols/mod.rs`'s `end_line`), so
`--insert-after '#package'` lands inside `[package]`, not after `[deps]`.

```console
$ lets edit t.toml --insert-after '#package' --new 'version = "2"'
── t.toml · inserted 1 line after #package (line 2) · check: toml ok · sha:0486752c92ba→9a6349c4cd25

```
